newsitem.title: INDIA: Tribals kill at least seven Indian soldiers.
newsitem.headline: Tribals kill at least seven Indian soldiers.

text.p: At least seven Indian soldiers were killed and three wounded in an ambush by unidentified guerrillas in the northeastern state of Manipur, police said.

S. Grewal, a senior police official, told Reuters that the guerrillas ambushed the vehicle carrying paramilitary soldiers near Wangchuk in the Thaubal district, some 40 km (30 miles) from the state capital Imphal.
Three wounded soldiers were taken to hospital, Grewal said.

Military officials in the eastern city of Calcutta said the ambush was probably the work of the Meitei tribe, a warrior community living in the highlands of the remote northeastern state bordering Burma.
Earlier six people were injured when a bomb exploded in the Thaubal district. The blast damaged a jeep, a motorcycle and three scooters.
The fresh outbreak of violence came on the third day of Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's five-day tour of the troubled region.
Gujral spent Wednesday in the neighbouring states of Meghalaya and Tripura and was expected in Manipur on Thursday.
A number of separatist groups, some tribal and others with Maoist ideologies, operate in the region's seven hilly states and accuse New Delhi of ignoring the area's economy.
The outlawed United Liberation Front of Asom (ULFA) called a general strike on Monday to protest against Gujral's visit to Assam state.
Gujral on Tuesday invited rebels for talks and promised a separate industrial policy to boost development.

The prime minister told a public meeting in Megahalaya on Wednesday that people in the northeast had an important role to play in defending national security. The northeast borders on Bangladesh, Bhutan, Burma and China.
Manipur has in recent years been torn by a violent secessionist campaign and savage inter-tribal warfare.
